note: Parse-time blowup, not execution: compileExpression() alone accounts for all of it, and the expression is REJECTED at the end (UNEXPECTED_TRAILING_TOKEN). Measured on prefixes of this source: 500 chars 1ms, 560 chars 2ms, 580 chars 1977ms, 600 chars 2096ms, 700 chars 8542ms, full 723 chars 17.9s. Nothing in the engine's safety set bounds it: maxExpressionLength is 2000, maxComplexity and maxNestingDepth are structural, and maxInstructions/maxStackDepth/the allocation budget all bound EXECUTION, which never starts. A host evaluating per keystroke freezes for seventeen seconds on 723 characters. Root construct not isolated: contiguous trimming from either end stops at ~510 characters, and the obvious suspects (unclosed brackets, long operator chains, comma lists, if/then/else, phrase operators) are all fast on their own. FIXED, root cause and not just the symptom. The construct was the labelled-line fallback in engine/ExpressionEngine.ts's parseExpression(): when a line does not parse whole, it retries the fragment after each COLON, rightmost first, and each retry re-entered the SAME function, which ran the whole fallback again on its own suffix. Those inner suffixes are exactly the ones the outer loop already visits (a colon at j > i gives slice(j+1), which the outer loop tries directly), so every level below the first re-attempted parses that had already failed, and each of those levels did it again: k colons compiled 2^k times. That is why trimming from either end stalled and why no single construct looked slow, the cost was in the number of colons, not in any one of them. Profiled with --cpu-prof: 96.3% of the 18 seconds was inside the EngineError constructor (Error.captureStackTrace), with 524,288 errors constructed and discarded for the 723-character case and 65,536 for a 500-character prefix, both exact powers of two. The retry now gets a plain parse with no fallback of its own, which loses no coverage. Measured after: 723 chars 3.0ms with 22 errors, the hang case 6.1ms with 22, and a synthetic worst case of 160 colons 3.6ms with 161 errors, i.e. linear.
